item.title: Hedge Funds’ Favorite US Bond Trade Is Sputtering
item.description: Hedge funds’ most popular trade in the US bond market is showing signs of maxing out.

item.title: Google Fined €890 Million in EU Over Search, App Store Breaches
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google was fined a total of €890 million ($1 billion) by the European Union for violating the bloc’s Digital Markets Act, in a decision that risks further inflaming tensions with US President Donald Trump.

item.title: Comcast Earnings Beat Estimates on Peacock, Box Office Successes
item.description: Comcast Corp. reported earnings that beat analysts’ estimates on key metrics, buoyed by the first-ever quarterly profitability at its Peacock streaming platform and a string of Hollywood hits.

item.title: Google Will Now Let Users Sign In to Accounts With a Selfie Video
item.description: Google is adding a selfie video option as a new way to sign in to accounts, providing an alternative for users who may be locked out due to a lost device or forgotten password.

item.title: Goldman Sachs, Absa See Ghana Rate Cuts Delayed by Iran War, Oil Prices
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Absa Group Ltd. believe the window for the Bank of Ghana to resume policy easing this year has closed due to fresh inflation pressures from renewed tensions in the Middle East

item.title: SpaceX Attempts Major Flight Test Again in Post-IPO Spotlight
item.description: SpaceX will again attempt a major test of its massive Starship rocket on Thursday after abandoning takeoff last week, exposing investors to the risks of the company’s rocky development cycle and heightening the stakes for the critical milestone.

item.title: Asian Oil Buyers in Talks With Saudis to Reroute Red Sea Flows
item.description: At least two Asian crude oil buyers are in talks with Saudi Aramco to potentially reroute flows around Africa after Houthi attacks on tankers in the Red Sea, according to traders familiar with the matter.

item.title: Victoria Plc Wins Support for Debt Deal After HSBC U-Turn
item.description: Troubled UK carpetmaker Victoria Plc secured enough bondholder support for a consensual debt restructuring after HSBC Holdings Plc backed the plan at the last minute, averting a costlier, more time-consuming court process.

item.title: BlackRock Says Elevated Yields Offer Bond Investors a Cushion
item.description: US Treasuries are offering investors solid protection against losses as yields remain elevated, according to BlackRock Inc.

item.title: Israel’s AI Czar Seeks Chip Fab, New Data Centers to Keep Edge
item.description: Israel is seeking to build up its chipmaking and artificial intelligence infrastructure, courting large US and Asian semiconductor producers and planning a major expansion of its data center capacity to preserve the country’s regional technological leadership.

item.title: Intel Needs More Than Blowout Earnings as Chips Rally Falters
item.description: Intel Corp. is expected to report strong second-quarter earnings after the market close Thursday, but even blowout results likely won’t be enough to reverse the stock’s July slide.

item.title: UAE Doubles Down on $1.4 Trillion US Pledge, Faults EU on Trade
item.description: The United Arab Emirates says it’s ahead of schedule with a plan to invest $1.4 trillion in the US over the next 10 years, and criticized the European Union for stalling trade talks.

item.title: PHP/USD: Marcos Confident Central Bank to Act on Weak Peso, Official Says
item.description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is confident that the central bank will act decisively on the peso, which weakened to the record low, according to the president’s press officer.

item.title: German Bond Yields Hit 15-Year High as Oil Spikes Before ECB
item.description: German bond yields rose to the highest level since 2011 as surging energy prices and mounting inflation expectations fueled bets on interest-rate hikes ahead of the European Central Bank’s decision later Thursday.

item.description: Mark Gurman on the state of play.

item.title: SK Hynix’s 51% Arbitrage Trade Stymied by Strict Conversion Cap
item.description: One of the world’s most enticing arbitrage opportunities will remain off limits.

item.title: China Tankers Head to Red Sea Chokepoint Despite Houthi Attacks
item.description: Two China-owned oil tankers loaded with Saudi Arabian crude are sticking to their course toward the Red Sea chokepoint of Bab el Mandeb, despite Houthi militants attacking vessels in the region overnight.

item.title: EasyJet Profit Falls 70% Amid Higher Fuel Bill, Lower Demand
item.description: EasyJet Plc said profit fell by 70% in its fiscal third quarter as the UK budget carrier continues to suffer from higher jet fuel costs and lower consumer demand, driven by the impact from the Middle East conflict.

item.title: BT Profit Falls as Broadband, Voice Margins Offset Cuts
item.description: BT Group Plc reported a slight decline in profits for its fiscal first quarter, as lower margins in its broadband and voice businesses offset its cost-cutting efforts.

item.title: Absa Nears Tanzania Deal to Combine $3 Billion of Banking Assets
item.description: Absa Group Ltd. is nearing a deal to combine its banking interests in Tanzania as the lender looks to increase the scale of its East African businesses, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: China Cuts AI Gap as Moonshot Shows Zhipu Isn’t One-Off, BI Says
item.description: Chinese AI models narrowed the performance gap with US counterparts to a record-low 6% in June, down from 9% in May, which Bloomberg Intelligence said raises questions about the sustainability of US technological supremacy in the sector.

item.title: TotalEnergies Profit Jumps 68% as War Upends Energy Markets
item.description: TotalEnergies SE said second-quarter profit surged as the Iran war boosted prices of crude and refined products, offsetting a drop in profits in its gas business.

item.title: Airtel Mobile-Money Unit Chooses London for Listing Location
item.description: Airtel Africa Plc picked London as the primary listing location for its mobile-money business and expects to start trading there this year.

item.title: AI Data Center Boom Sparks 80% Surge in First-Half FDI Applications to Thailand
item.description: Foreign investors applied to invest 1.37 trillion baht ($40.6 billion) in Thailand in the first half of 2026, up 80% from a year earlier, amid a wave of investments in artificial intelligence and data center projects.

item.title: Hong Kong, Malaysia Collaborate to Broaden Cross-Market Access
item.description: Hong Kong and Malaysia will work together to expand access to capital and deepen cross-border participation in both markets as they look to attract more international investment.

item.title: China Curbs Loan Structure Widely Used by Distressed Developers
item.description: China is restricting real estate companies from using a popular offshore loan structure that has helped some of them weather the country’s property crisis, according to people familiar with the matter, adding to recent moves to strengthen oversight of overseas borrowing.

item.title: Roche Quarterly Sales Held Back by Blockbuster Eye Drug
item.description: Roche Holding’s results showed a slower-than-expected recovery for eye blockbuster Vabysmo as investors look to a key new drug to power growth ahead.

item.title: Burnham Cuts Business Rates on Pubs, Clubs and Live Venues
item.description: The UK will cut tax on pubs, social clubs and some live music venues across England, as new Prime Minister Andy Burnham marks his first week in power with a string of promises to lower the cost of living.
